sec: Wilson's neurological signs, K-F rings and multi-organ pathology

items.q: What is the most common (m/c) clinical neurological manifestation in Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Under classical neurological manifestations, item 4 lists 'Dysarthria (m/c)'. (Book p1015)

items.q: Match each neurological feature of Wilson's disease with its clinical sign — 1) Facial grimacing posturing 2) Coarse arm tremor … A) Wing-beating tremors B) Risus sardonicus (dysphonic vacuous posturing)
items.exp: Facial dystonia manifests as 'Dysphonic posturing (Risus sardonicus)', and tremor presents as 'Wing beating tremors'. (Book p1015)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a rare neurological manifestation of Wilson's disease on this page?
items.exp: Rare neurological features listed are ANS involvement, memory loss, and migraine; trigeminal neuralgia is not mentioned. (Book p1015)

items.q: Fill up: In Wilson's disease, the Kayser-Fleischer (K-F) ring is caused by copper deposition in the ______ membrane of the cornea near the limbus.
items.exp: The K-F ring is defined as 'Cu2+ deposits in descemet membrane near limbus especially in superior and inferior poles.' (Book p1015)

items.q: What respective association rates are documented for corneal copper rings in patients presenting with liver versus brain disease?
items.exp: K-F ring association is 60–65% in hepatic presentations and 95–99% in neurological presentations. (Book p1015)

items.q: Besides Wilson's disease, in which of the following cholestatic conditions can a corneal Kayser-Fleischer ring occasionally be seen?
items.exp: K-F rings can occur in prolonged cholestasis: Wilson's, PBC, PSC, and Familial cholestatic syndrome; not in acute hepatitis A. (Book p1015)

items.q: What characteristic lens abnormality is produced by copper deposition in Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Item 2 under ophthalmic findings is 'Sunflower cataract'. (Book p1015)

items.q: Match each organ system with its extrahepatic manifestation in Wilson's disease — 1) Endocrine 2) Renal 3) Blood … A) Proximal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type-2 RTA) B) Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia C) Hypoparathyroidism
items.exp: Other manifestations: Endocrine = Hypoparathyroid; Renal = Proximal RTA Type-2; Blood = Coombs negative hemolysis. (Book p1015)

items.q: Which gastrointestinal organ complication is listed among the systemic manifestations of Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Under other manifestations, the 'GI' branch lists 'Pancreatitis'. (Book p1015)

items.q: Assess the two statements on Wilson's disease: I Kayser-Fleischer rings characteristically disappear or regress following effective copper chelation therapy. II Wilson's disease produces distal Type-1 renal tubular acidosis with nephrocalcinosis.
items.exp: Statement I is true ('Rx: Chelation therapy' leads to regression). Statement II is false because Wilson's produces Proximal RTA Type-2 (Fanconi syndrome). (Book p1015)

items.q: A 19-year-old woman presents with secondary amenorrhea, a history of two spontaneous abortions, dysarthria, and bilateral wing-beating tremor. Slit-lamp biomicroscopy reveals a golden-brown ring at the superior and inferior limbus. What is the definitive initial medical management?
items.exp: The clinical picture demonstrates neurological Wilson's disease with K-F ring, managed with chelation therapy. (Book p1015)
